Consult Summary:
- 26-year-old woman with 3-day history of worsening headache, right peri-orbital predominant with photophobia and visual phenomena; suspected migraine. Analgesic options discussed; advised follow-up and safety-netting.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Headache for ~3 days, worsening.
- Characteristics: Constant with fluctuations; predominately around right eye but “all over” at times; dull with intermittent sharp pains; gradual onset; rated 8/10; began at work.
- Associated symptoms: Photophobia; initial episode of “shooting lights”; nausea without vomiting; difficulty focusing.
- Pertinent negatives: No vision loss; no speech disturbance; no limb weakness; no fever; no rash; no head trauma. Neck pain/stiffness: patient said “yeah” then “no” (conflict noted).
- Prior episodes: Past headaches typically relieved by ibuprofen; current episode not relieved.
- Medications tried: Ibuprofen over last 2 days, “3 tablets/day”; tablet strength and exact dosing not documented; minimal benefit.
- Past medical history: None reported.
- Family history: Mother and sister with migraines (mother’s severe, seasonal triggers).
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Regular medications: None reported.
- Social history: Works in IT with prolonged screen time; uses glasses; no recent eye exam. Social smoker; social alcohol use.
- Preventive care: Not discussed.

Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Physical exam: Not documented.

Impression:
- Suspected migraine-type headache given unilateral peri-orbital predominance, photophobia, visual phenomena, nausea, and family history.

Plan:
- Analgesia:
  - Education on ibuprofen dosing: up to 2 tablets three times daily (exact tablet strength not documented).
  - Discussed prescribing a stronger NSAID (naproxen; dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Discussed adding acetaminophen/paracetamol or codeine (doses/routes/frequencies not documented).
- Monitoring/records: Keep a headache diary to identify triggers.
- Follow-up: Return in 1–2 weeks to reassess; consider prophylactic therapy if headaches recur/frequent.
- Safety-netting: Seek urgent review if worsening headache, new vision problems, weakness, or feeling generally unwell.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals; neurological exam; fundoscopic/eye exam; pregnancy/contraception status (question about “pill” unanswered); detailed dosing and specific prescriptions not fully documented; allergy verification limited to “none known.”
- Internal conflicts: Neck pain/stiffness—patient initially said “yeah” then “no” (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; some pauses/ambiguities and one conflicting response.
